{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Judith Victor Grabiner''' (born October 12, 1938) is an [[Americans|American]] [[mathematician]] and [[history of mathematics|historian of mathematics]], who is Flora Sanborn Pitzer Professor Emerita of Mathematics at [[Pitzer College]], one of the [[Claremont Colleges]].<ref name=pitzer>{{cite web |url=https://www.pitzer.edu/academics/faculty/judith-grabiner/ |title=Judith V. Grabiner |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=October 12, 2016 |website=Faculty Directory and Profiles |publisher=Pitzer College |access-date=October 4, 2017 }}</ref> Her main interest is in mathematics in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.<ref>{{cite book|author=Ronald Calinger|title=Vita Mathematica: Historical Research and Integration with Teaching|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=D21wKHoYGg0C&pg=PA340|date=1 January 1996|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-0-88385-097-8|pages=340}}</ref>

==Education==
Grabiner completed a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree at the [[University of Chicago]] in 1960. She was a graduate student in the [[history of science]] at [[Harvard University]], completing a [[Master of Arts]] in 1962 and a [[Ph.D.]] in 1966, under [[I. Bernard Cohen]].<ref name=cv>{{cite web |url=https://www.pitzer.edu/academics/wp-content/uploads/sites/38/2014/12/FAC-CV-Judy-Grabiner.pdf |title=Short Curriculum Vitae: Judith Victor Grabiner |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=April 2012 |website=Profile: Judith V. Grabiner |publisher=Pitzer College |access-date=October 4, 2017 |archive-date=October 5, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171005151601/https://www.pitzer.edu/academics/wp-content/uploads/sites/38/2014/12/FAC-CV-Judy-Grabiner.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>  Her PhD dissertation was on Italian mathematician [[Joseph-Louis Lagrange]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://id.lib.harvard.edu/aleph/003842904/catalog |title=The calculus as algebra: J.-L. LaGrange, 1736-1813. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=1966 |website=Harvard University Library |publisher=Harvard University |access-date=October 4, 2017 }}</ref>

==Career==
Grabiner was an instructor at Harvard for several years, before she and her husband Sandy Grabiner moved to California.<ref>{{cite news |last=Tsang |first=Derek |date=March 2014 |title=Beauty in numbers |url=https://mag.uchicago.edu/science-medicine/beauty-numbers |work=University of Chicago Magazine |location=Chicago |access-date=October 4, 2017 }}</ref> She was a professor of history at [[California State University, Dominguez Hills]] from 1972 to 1985.<ref name=cv/>

Grabiner joined the mathematics department at [[Pitzer College]] in 1985, and has been the [[Russell K. Pitzer|Flora Sanborn Pitzer]] Professor of Mathematics since 1994.<ref name=pitzer/> Her teaching includes courses on the [[history of mathematics]], mathematics in different cultures, and [[Philosophy of mathematics|mathematics and philosophy]].<ref name=pitzer/>

==Recognition==
Grabiner received the [[Carl B. Allendoerfer Award]] for the best article in ''[[Mathematics Magazine]]'' in 1984, 1989, and 1996, and the [[Lester R. Ford]] Award in 1984, 1998, 2005, and 2010, for the best article in ''[[American Mathematical Monthly]]''.<ref>[http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/carl-b-allendoerfer-awards Mathematical Association of America – Carl B. Allendoerfer Awards]</ref><ref>[http://www.maa.org/news/math-news/judith-grabiner-wins-maas-ford-award-for-the-fourth-time Mathematical Association of America – Judith Grabiner Wins MAA's Ford Award for the Fourth Time]</ref>

In 2003, Grabiner received one of the [[Mathematical Association of America]]'s [[Deborah and Franklin Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thegreatcourses.com/professors/judith-v-grabiner/ |title=Professor Judith V. Grabiner, Ph.D. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2017 |website=The Great Courses |publisher= The Teaching Company, LLC |access-date=October 4, 2017 }}</ref> She became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2012.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-01-19.</ref> In 2014, she was awarded the [[Edwin F. Beckenbach|Beckenbach]] Book Prize.<ref>[http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/beckenbach-book-prize Mathematical Association of America – Beckenbach Book Prize]</ref>

She was the 2021 winner of the [[Albert Leon Whiteman Memorial Prize]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for her outstanding contributions to the history of mathematics, in particular her works on Cauchy, Lagrange, and MacLaurin; her widely-recognized gift for expository writing; and a distinguished career of teaching, lecturing, and numerous publications promoting a better understanding of mathematics and the significant roles it plays in culture generally".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blogs.ams.org/beyondreviews/2021/01/03/jmm-prizes-and-awards-2021/|title=JMM Prizes and Awards 2021|first=Edward|last=Dunne|publisher=American Mathematical Society}}</ref>
